verification.note: migrated from data/antibiogram-raw.json: extracted from the source PDF, then re-verified cell by cell by a second reader (2026). Method: Tables 2 to 4 (pages 5 and 6) print sensitive, intermediate and resistant counts and percentages; only % sensitive was entered, as printed. The separate MRSA table (Table 4) was not merged into the S. aureus row. Ceftazidime was tested on 45 P. aeruginosa isolates; amikacin in the discussion rests on 26 isolates.

notes: Sammal et al. (Cureus 2024) studied ear discharge from patients with chronic suppurative otitis media at Government Doon Medical College, Dehradun, August 2022 to January 2024: 129 culture-positive isolates, tested by VITEK 2 with CLSI breakpoints. Only P. aeruginosa (46 isolates) and S. aureus (23) have full antibiograms. Figures are % susceptible as printed; intermediate results are not counted as susceptible. The S. aureus figures cover the 23 isolates of the paper's S. aureus table; the 18 MRSA isolates had a separate table and are not included, so MRSA made up about 43.9% of all S. aureus. Some drugs were tested on fewer isolates (for example piperacillin-tazobactam 38, imipenem 44). P. aeruginosa amikacin (57.8%) comes from the paper's discussion, not its table, and the cefoperazone figure is cefoperazone-sulbactam.
